'''Kai no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (甲斐国造, also read as Kai Koku-zō) was the {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} governing {{ill|Kai Province|en|Kai Province|qid=Q858076|lt=Kai Province|1=Kai Province}}.
__TOC__{{-}}
== Overview ==
=== Name ===
The title appears as '''Kai no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' in the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}, the {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi|1=Kujiki}} "Kuni no Miyatsuko Chronicles," and the {{ill|Shokeifu|ja|諸系譜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokeifu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref>{{ill|Suzuki Manen|ja|鈴木真年}}, "Tōgoku Shokokuzō," ''Shokeizu'' Vol. 1.</ref><ref name="nakata">{{ill|Nakata Kenshin|ja|中田憲信}}, "Kai no Kuni no Miyatsuko," ''Shokeizu'' Vol. 7.</ref>
=== Ancestors ===
According to the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}, the lineage traces back to Emperor Kaika, who took Princess {{ill|Oketsuhime|ja|意祁都比売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oketsuhime|1=Oketsu-hime no mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97496338}} of the {{ill|Wani clan|ja|和邇氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 和珥氏|1=Wani clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11417873}} lineage as consort. Their son, {{ill|Hikoimasu no Ōkimi|lt=Hikoimasu no Ōkimi|lt=Hikozatsuo|ja|彦坐王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikozatsuo|qq=}}, married Princess {{ill|Saho no Ōkurami to Me|ja|沙本之大闇見戸売|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saho no Ōkurami to Me|1=Saho no Ōkuramito-me|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q13360104}}, giving birth to {{ill|Saho no Hikoo|ja|沙本毘子王|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saho no Hikoo|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, considered the ancestor of Kai no Kuni no Miyatsuko and the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan|qq=}}.

The {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi|1=Kujiki}} records that during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ja|景行天皇|lt=Emperor Keikō|lt_ja=景行朝}}, {{ill|Shiomi no Sukune|ja|塩海宿禰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiomi no Sukune|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 塩海足尼}}, a 4th-generation descendant and son of Omishitsuhiko-no-Kimi (3rd-generation descendant of Saho no Hikoo), was appointed the first Kai no Kuni no Miyatsuko.
=== Clan ===
The ruling clan, '''{{ill|Kai clan|ja|甲斐氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kai clan|1=Q11577901|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11577901}}''', bore the {{ill|Kabane|ja|姓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabane|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of {{ill|Kimi (kabane)|lt=Kimi (kabane)|lt=Kimi|ja|君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kimi|qq=}}. The claim of imperial descent has been a subject of scholarly debate (see [[#Studies|Studies]]).
=== Studies ===
==== Clan and Kabane of the Kuni no Miyatsuko ====
In the latter half of the 5th century to the 6th century, farmers and professional groups ruled by local chieftains were organized into units of "be," forming the {{ill|bemin system|ja|部民制}} in which "be" held by local magnates were governed by central magnates and ''tomo-no-miyatsuko'' who provided tributes and corvée. The kuni no miyatsuko system — a hereditary position appointed by the {{ill|Yamato court|ja|大和王権|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato court|ja_comment=|2=ja|3=ヤマト王権|1=Yamato Kingship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2658252}} over local magnates to govern provincial be — developed in parallel.

In {{ill|Kai Province|en|Kai Province|qid=Q858076|lt=Kai Province|1=Kai Province}}, ink-inscribed textiles from {{ill|Shōsōin|en|Shōsōin|qid=Q2379007|lt=Shōsōin|1=Shōsōin}} and ink-marked pottery unearthed from the Ōhara Ruins in {{ill|Fuefuki|en|Fuefuki|qid=Q849434|lt=Fuefuki City|1=Fuefuki}} confirm the presence of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan|qq=}} in Yamanashi District. {{ill|Seki Akira|ja|関晃}} estimated their {{ill|kabane|ja|姓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kabane|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} as {{ill|Atai (kabane)|ja|直 (姓)|lt=Atai|lt_ja=直}}, common among local magnates, considering them in a same-clan relationship with other be-managing clans in Kai Province — the commonly accepted position. {{ill|Suzuki Masanobu|ja|鈴木正信}} alternatively proposed "Kai-no-Atai" based on the Nijō-Ōji wooden tablet bearing "Sadaitoneri Kai □" and the pattern of other kuni no miyatsuko clan names bearing place names of their jurisdiction. Neither position can be confirmed from extant historical sources.
==== Relationships with Other Regions ====
The construction of {{ill|Kai Chōshizuka Kofun|en|Kai Chōshizuka Kofun|qid=Q11577925|lt=Kai Chōshizuka Kofun|1=Kai Chōshizuka Kofun}} in the 4th century indicates strong ties to the Yamato royal court. This connection is further substantiated by the discovery of {{ill|Sankakubuchi Shinjūkyō|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sankakubuchi Shinjūkyō|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=}} in the area.
== Base of Power ==
Shiomi no Sukune and subsequent rulers were centered consistently in the northern {{ill|Yamanashi District|ja|山梨郡}}, in the area from around present-day {{ill|Fuefuki|en|Fuefuki|qid=Q849434|lt=Fuefuki City|1=Fuefuki}} to the eastern part of {{ill|Kōfu|en|Kōfu|qid=Q201932|lt=Kōfu|1=Kōfu}}.<ref name="houga2" />
=== Domain ===
Since no other kuni no miyatsuko was established in {{ill|Kai Province|en|Kai Province|qid=Q858076|lt=Kai Province|1=Kai Province}}, the Kai no Kuni no Miyatsuko likely governed the entirety of the province.
== Clan Shrines ==
The clan's primary shrine was '''{{ill|Asama Shrine (Fuefuki)|ja|浅間神社 (笛吹市)|lt=Asama Shrine|lt_ja=浅間神社}}''', the {{ill|ichi-no-miya|ja|一宮}} of {{ill|Kai Province|en|Kai Province|qid=Q858076|lt=Kai Province|1=Kai Province}}.
=== Related Shrines ===
* {{ill|Tamamoro Shrine|ja|玉諸神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamamoro Shrine|qq=}} (''tamamoro-jinja''): A Shikinai rongi shrine in {{ill|Kōfu|en|Kōfu|qid=Q201932|lt=Kōfu|1=Kōfu}}, associated with the second ruler, Hayahiko no Sukune. The former enshrinement site was called Mimuroyama.
* {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|lt=Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|lt=Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki)|ja|美和神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki)|qq=}} (''miwa-jinja''): A Shikinai rongi shrine in {{ill|Fuefuki|en|Fuefuki|qid=Q849434|lt=Fuefuki City|1=Fuefuki}}, founded when Shiomi no Sukune served as chief ritualist under Emperor Keikō's orders.
* {{ill|Kaina Shrine|ja|甲斐奈神社}} (''kaina-jinja''): Three Shikinai rongi shrines exist. Doi-Moto-biko-no-Ōkimi, ancestor of the kuni no miyatsuko, is said to have started the worship.
* {{ill|Saku Shrine|ja|佐久神社}} (''saku-jinja''): A Shikinai rongi shrine in Kōfu City. Founded after the kofun of Doi-Moto-biko-no-Ōkimi was re-interred from Ōmiyayama to Tenjinyama, at the original site.
* {{ill|Kanazakura Shrine|ja|金櫻神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanazakura Shrine|qq=}} (''kanazakura-jinja''): A Shikinai rongi shrine in Kōfu City. Founded when Shiomi no Sukune was ordered to construct the shrine buildings during Emperor Keikō's reign.
* {{ill|Kanazakura Shrine (Yamanashi)|ja|金櫻神社 (山梨市)|lt=Kanazakura Shrine|lt_ja=金櫻神社}} (''kanazakura-jinja''): A Shikinai rongi shrine in {{ill|Yamanashi, Yamanashi|ja|山梨市|lt=Yamanashi City|lt_ja=山梨市}}. Founded when Shiomi no Sukune invited the Hashidate Myōjin from {{ill|Amanohashidate|ja|天橋立}}.
=== Burial Sites ===
* '''{{ill|Ōmaruyama Kofun|en|Ōmaruyama Kofun|qid=Q11431880|lt=Ōmaruyama Kofun|1=Ōmaruyama Kofun}}''' (''ōmaruyama-kofun''): A {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} in {{ill|Kōfu|en|Kōfu|qid=Q201932|lt=Kōfu|1=Kōfu}}, possibly the tomb of Omishitsuhiko-no-Mikoto (father of Shiomi no Sukune), from its mid-4th century construction.
* '''{{ill|Kai Chōshizuka Kofun|en|Kai Chōshizuka Kofun|qid=Q11577925|lt=Kai Chōshizuka Kofun|1=Kai Chōshizuka Kofun}}''' (''kai chōshizuka-kofun''): A keyhole-shaped kofun in Kōfu City, possibly the tomb of Shiomi no Sukune, the first kuni no miyatsuko, from its late 4th century construction.
* '''{{ill|Tenjinyama Kofun (Kōfu)|ja|天神山古墳 (甲府市)|lt=Tenjinyama Kofun|lt_ja=天神山古墳}}''' (''tenjinyama-kofun''): A keyhole-shaped kofun in Kōfu City, possibly the tomb of Hayahiko no Sukune, the second kuni no miyatsuko, from its 4th century construction.
== Notable Figures ==
* '''{{ill|Shiomi no Sukune|ja|塩海足尼|1=Shiomi no Sukune|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiomi no Sukune|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiomi no Sukune|qq=}}''': The first ruler, credited with founding several shrines and establishing Kai Province's governance.
